jobs.description:
Position Title

Director, People and Culture Strategy

Employment Type

Permanent

Existing Vacancy

Yes

Division/Branch

People and Culture Division / People and Culture Strategy

Application Deadline

September 25, 2026

Pay Level

13

Pay Range

$149,307 to $186,631

Work Location:

Head Office, Toronto, ON; (In-Office)

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO)
is an agency where innovation thrives, ideas flourish, and passion drives us to new heights of excellence. Reporting to the Ministry of the Attorney General, the AGCO is responsible for regulating Ontario’s vibrant alcohol, gaming, horse racing, and private retail cannabis sectors in accordance with the principles of honesty and integrity, and in the public interest.

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) is seeking a strategic, collaborative and forward-thinking leader to serve as Director, People and Culture Strategy. Reporting to the Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO), the Director People and Culture Strategy provides enterprise leadership for People and Culture strategy, transformation and modernization, with responsibility for advancing the People Strategic Plan, divisional priorities, enterprise metrics and executive reporting, HR digital enablement, responsible AI adoption, diversity, inclusion and accessibility (DI&A), inclusive leadership and high-performing team leadership.

This role translates enterprise and divisional priorities into practical strategies, roadmaps, implementation plans, performance measures and governance mechanisms that strengthen organizational readiness, workforce planning, evidence-based decision-making and measurable impact across AGCO.

The ideal candidate is a trusted strategic advisor who brings strong judgment, systems thinking and a collaborative leadership style. They are comfortable operating in a complex public-sector environment, balancing long-term transformation with immediate operational priorities, and translating data, risk, workforce trends and stakeholder needs into practical, inclusive and measurable people strategies.

If you are motivated by the opportunity to lead strategic HR transformation, advance responsible digital and AI adoption, strengthen diversity, inclusion and accessibility, and support a strong employee experience, this role offers a meaningful platform to make a lasting enterprise-wide contribution at AGCO.

What You Will Do

Lead the development, implementation and ongoing refresh of AGCO’s People Strategic Plan, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities, government mandates, workforce risks and evolving organizational needs.
Translate organizational priorities into actionable people strategies, roadmaps, initiatives, performance measures and implementation plans.
Oversee the planning, prioritization and delivery of People and Culture initiatives, projects and divisional priorities that advance organizational goals.
Establish planning, governance, reporting and accountability mechanisms to monitor progress against strategic commitments and demonstrate measurable impact.
Provide strategic advice to the CHRO, C-Suite, senior leaders and governance committees on HR priorities, workforce implications, transformation risks and organizational readiness.
Design and oversee enterprise People and Culture performance indicators, dashboards, workforce analytics and executive reporting to support transparency, accountability and evidence-informed decision-making.
Lead HR digital enablement and responsible AI adoption by developing practical capability, governance practices and high-value use cases that improve service quality, efficiency and decision-making.
Provide enterprise leadership for DI&A strategy, accessibility and inclusive leadership, embedding inclusion principles into AGCO culture, operations and people practices.
Lead the refresh, implementation and evaluation of enterprise DI&A strategy, including the development and reporting of meaningful performance measures.
Act as a senior subject matter expert on DI&A and accessibility, advising executives and senior leaders on inclusive talent practices, cultural transformation and emerging obligations.
Provide leadership and direction to a team by setting clear expectations, prioritizing deliverables, supporting development and fostering a culture of inclusion, accountability, learning and high

You Have

Post-secondary education in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Organizational Psychology, Adult Education, Strategic Planning, Leadership, Human Rights, Public Policy or a related field, or equivalent work experience; a master’s degree is considered an asset.
Minimum of 8 years progressive leadership experience in strategic planning, organizational transformation, HR strategy, performance measurement, workforce analytics, DI&A, accessibility, digital enablement and/or related areas.
Demonstrated ability to translate enterprise priorities into practical strategies, roadmaps, governance structures, implementation plans and measurable outcomes.
Strong understanding of HR digital adoption, HRIS-enabled process improvement, workflow automation, workforce analytics, digital service delivery, change management and responsible AI use.
Knowledge of HR data governance, privacy, accessibility, security, records management and ethical use of workforce information.
Experience developing executive-level reports, dashboards, briefings and presentations that translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations.
Strong consultation, facilitation, public speaking and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence and build alignment across senior leaders, governance bodies and cross-functional partners.
Demonstrated experience leading DI&A strategy, accessibility initiatives, inclusive leadership development, employee engagement forums, committees or enterprise-wide measurement frameworks.
Strong knowledge of Ontario legal and regulatory frameworks related to human rights, accessibility, employment standards and inclusive workplace practices.
Experience leading, coaching and developing teams in a complex, unionized and public-sector environment is an asset.
Eligibility to work in Canada and the ability to successfully complete a criminal background check.

To apply to this vacancy, please submit your application online at our Careers webpage located at Careers | Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario by September 25, 2026.
Please note that only applications submitted through the Applicant Tracking System will be accepted.

About The AGCO

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) is an Ontario provincial regulatory agency that reports to the Ministry of the Attorney General. We are responsible for regulating the alcohol, gaming, horse racing and cannabis retail sectors in accordance with the principles of honesty and integrity, and in the public interest.

The AGCO is proud to be recognized as one of Greater Toronto’s Top Employers for the second year in a row. This annual distinction reflects our commitment to cultivating a workplace environment that prioritizes employee well-being, emphasizing work-life balance, mental health resources, and opportunities for professional growth. We remain committed to fostering a supportive and rewarding work environment for our employees.

What We Offer

The AGCO provides a comprehensive range of benefits and programs (subject to eligibility), including:

Generous time-off policy, including 2 volunteer days to contribute to causes that matter to you.
Defined benefit pension plans to secure your financial future.
Comprehensive health, dental, and vision plans, with 100% employer-paid premiums.
Well-being credits to support gym memberships, therapy, financial planning, and more.
Employer-paid parental leave top-up.
Professional development opportunities with access to training programs, leadership resources, and reimbursement for professional memberships.
24/7 confidential support through our Employee Assistance Program.
Convenient, central location near the subway line for easy access when working in the office. Paid onsite parking is also available.

Please note that only applications submitted through the Applicant Tracking System will be accepted.

The AGCO is an inclusive and equal opportunity employer.

The AGCO has the responsibility to lead by example in advancing racial equity and to build a diverse, inclusive, accessible and respectful workplace where every employee has a voice and the opportunity to fully contribute. To this effect, you are encouraged to reflect upon the diversity you would bring to the role within your application including, but not limited to, individuals identifying with one or more of the under-represented groups identified within Ontario’s Human Rights Code. 

Disability related accommodation during the recruitment process is available upon request. Persons with disabilities who require accommodation during the application process, or who need job postings in an alternative format, may email their request to askhr@agco.ca. The subject line should read “Accommodation in Application – [Position Title].

We do not use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to screen, assess, or select applicants at any stage of the hiring process. All applications will be reviewed and evaluated by our Human Resources team and hiring managers.

Position Summary

Reporting to the CEO, the Director, Finance will be an important and integral part of the Leadership Team. Director, Finance will lead Dixon Hall's financial management function, providing strategic and operational oversight of accounting, budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and internal controls across the Agency. The Director ensures the financial integrity of Dixon Hall's operations, safeguards its resources, and provides senior management and the Board with the financial insight needed to support sound decision-making in service of Dixon Hall's mission.

The Director, Finance will also liaise with the Board and participate in Board meetings, work with the Chair of the Finance Audit and Risk Committee, and other Board committees as required; undertake and update the Risk portfolio for the agency and manage the finance department in the areas of accounts payable; confirm the accuracy of monthly remittances; record deposits to accounts receivable as well as; you will be responsible for the annual audit working papers and the work required by the finance department to coordinate the annual audit as well as ensuring timely and accurate invoicing; update and maintain the accuracy of the internal database(s); ensure the completion of all administrative duties related to the Finance Department.

Duties And Responsibilities

Strategic Financial Leadership

Serve as Dixon Hall's senior financial strategist, translating the Agency's mission and strategic plan into a sound, sustainable financial framework
Advise the CEO and Board on the financial implications of strategic decisions, including program expansion, new funding opportunities, and organizational risk
Build and maintain Dixon Hall's financial sustainability strategy, including reserve fund policy, revenue diversification, and long-term capital planning
Monitor the regulatory and funding landscape (provincial, federal, and municipal) affecting the non-profit and charitable sector, and advise leadership on emerging risks and opportunities

Budgeting, Forecasting & Financial Planning

Lead Agency-wide operational and capital budgeting and forecasting processes, aligning departmental budgets to strategic priorities
Analyze cost and revenue performance against budget across all programs and funding streams to assess financial performance and risk
Investigate budget and reporting variances and lead corrective action in partnership with program leadership
Identify and act on opportunities for cost efficiency and revenue growth across the Agency

Fund Accounting, Funder & Grant Compliance (NPO-specific)

Oversee fund accounting practices to ensure accurate tracking and reporting of restricted and unrestricted funding across all programs and funders (municipal, provincial, federal, and philanthropic)
Ensure compliance with individual funder reporting requirements and deadlines, including government funding agreements administered through Ontario Health Teams and other current provincial/municipal funding bodies
Oversee the integrity of client billing, fee revenue, and accounts receivable processes across program areas, ensuring accurate reconciliation between program systems (e.g., CIMS) and the Agency's accounting system
Oversee the accuracy and timeliness of donation processing and reconciliation between the donor database (e.g., SUMAC) and the accounting system, in partnership with Fund Development

Financial Reporting, Governance & Risk Management

Prepare and present financial statements, variance analyses, and strategic financial reporting to the CEO, Board, and Finance/Audit Committee
Ensure the adequacy and ongoing effectiveness of internal controls across all financial processes
Develop, monitor, and enforce financial policies and procedures governing accounting, budgeting, forecasting, and project/program tracking
Lead the annual external audit process and serve as primary liaison to the Agency's auditors
Ensure timely and accurate charitable regulatory filings (including the CRA T3010 Registered Charity Information Return) and compliance with all applicable non-profit financial regulations

Financial Systems Modernization & Automation

Lead the modernization of Dixon Hall's financial systems and processes, identifying opportunities to automate manual, repetitive tasks (e.g., billing reconciliation, revenue posting, payroll allocation, donation reconciliation) currently performed across CIMS, ADAGIO, and SUMAC
Champion the adoption of integrated, cloud-based financial and reporting tools that reduce manual data entry, minimize reconciliation errors, and free up Finance team capacity for higher-value analysis and strategic support
Evaluate and recommend automation opportunities in funder reporting, program cost allocation, and month-end close processes, balancing efficiency gains against cost, staff capacity, and data security requirements
Partner with IT and external vendors to scope, implement, and change-manage new financial systems or automation tools, ensuring proper internal controls and audit trails are maintained throughout
Build the Finance team's digital capability, ensuring staff are trained and equipped to work effectively with new tools and systems as automation is introduced

Payroll & Vendors & CRA Financial Oversight

Ensure accurate accrual and allocation of payroll & vendor costs, including benefits allocation by program and funding source
Oversee accurate program-based cost allocation for government and third-party funded positions
Ensure payroll-related financial reporting (including CRA remittance reconciliation) is accurate and current
Ensure CRA compliance on all financial matters

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, develop, and supervise the Finance department, fostering a culture of accuracy, accountability, and continuous improvement
Hire, train, coach, and formally evaluate Finance team members
Build team capability to support the Agency's growing scale and complexity

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Organizational Impact

Partners with Directors and program leaders across Dixon Hall to ensure financial decisions support — and are informed by — operational and client-service realities
Champion a client-focused, mission-driven approach to financial management, recognizing Finance's role in enabling Dixon Hall's community impact
Drive process improvements and technology modernization (accounting systems, reporting tools) to increase efficiency and data reliability across the Agency

Qualifications

CPA, CGA, College Diploma in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or a related field or equivalent senior level financial experience
10-15 years of experience in Finance with 10 years in managerial positions
Ability to oversee and manage teams
Experience with budgets, accounting, and reporting systems
Strong working knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles
Proficiency with a variety of accounting software, CIMS for billings and SUMAC accounting software and spreadsheet programs and applications
Effective attention to detail and a high degree of accuracy
Ability to build and maintain lasting internal and external relationships
High level of proficiency with Microsoft Office productivity suite
Knowledge and experience with office operational equipment
Experience with not for profit funding and reporting
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a strong ability to exchange knowledge
Strong verbal and written English language communication skills; fluency in additional languages, relevant to the Agency’s communities of service, will be considered an asset
Must be qualified to work in Canada legally for the employer
Able to provide a Vulnerable Sector Screening check with a ‘Clear’ or satisfactory result that meets the operational requirements of the Agency

Working Conditions

Modern office workspace illuminated by either fluorescent, LED, incandescent, or natural light sources
Able to access older buildings and workspaces that have not been converted to meet current accessibility standards
Quiet to moderate noise levels that are consistent with a modern office space in which multiple employees work simultaneously
Overtime as required

Physical and Sensory Demands

Long periods spent at a desk/computer
Manual dexterity required to use desktop computer and peripherals
Able to tolerate a variety of indoor environments as determined by program location
Mobility will be a key component of this position in order to address the needs of our Agency locations and programs

Direct Reports

Controller
Manager, Finance
Financial Analyst
Financial and Administration Analyst
Accounts Payable

Dixon Hall may use Artificial Intelligence-assisted tools during the recruitment process to support efficiency and consistency. Final hiring decisions are made by the Human Resources team.

Dixon Hall is dedicated to fostering an inclusive selection process and work environment, guided by their Race Relations and Employment Equity Policies. If selected for an interview, please inform the hiring manager or the People and Culture team at peopleandculture@dixonhall.org of any accommodations you may require during the interview process.

To achieve their goal of inclusivity and diversity, Dixon Hall actively seeks exceptional candidates from varied backgrounds and with lived experiences. Individuals who self-identify as being from marginalized communities, including Indigenous peoples, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, and those from the 2SLGBTQIA+ community or who have experienced homelessness, are strongly encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance & Corporate Development
jobs.description:
Job Description

Full-Time • London, Ontario

S.E.M. Construction is entering a new era of growth, expanding our capabilities, strengthening our market position, and exploring strategic opportunities across Southwestern Ontario. We’re seeking a Vice President of Finance & Corporate Development with deep construction-industry expertise and a proven track record in M&A strategy, execution, and integration. This executive will strengthen our financial foundation and help shape the future of S.E.M. alongside our CEO and leadership team. Core Mandate Lead all financial operations at S.E.M. while architecting long-term financial strategy. Oversee accounting, reporting, forecasting, capital planning, and risk management, and serve as the strategic driver behind acquisition evaluation, negotiation, and integration.
Key Responsibilities Financial Leadership & Strategy

• Lead the full finance function, including accounting, budgeting, forecasting, treasury, and financial reporting.
• Develop and execute long-term financial strategies aligned with corporate growth objectives. • Provide clear, data-driven insights to the CEO and executive team.
• Oversee cash flow management, capital allocation, and investment planning.
• Strengthen financial systems, controls, and processes to support scalability.
Construction Finance Accountability The Controller leads the day-to-day execution of the finance function. The Vice President provides executive oversight and remains accountable for the following:
• Job costing, WIP reporting, margin analysis, and project financial performance.
• Bonding, insurance, and financial compliance requirements appropriate to a mid-sized or large construction firm.
• The quality and reliability of forecasting, risk assessment, and project profitability information provided to operations and estimating.
• The financial performance of multi-sector construction portfolios, including IC&I, MURB, healthcare, and special projects. Mergers, Acquisitions & Corporate Development
• Identify and evaluate acquisition targets aligned with S.E.M.’s strategic direction.
• Lead financial due diligence, valuation modelling, and deal structuring.
• Partner with legal, tax, and external advisors to manage negotiations and transaction execution.
• Build integration plans that protect culture, retain talent, and accelerate value creation. • Assess post-acquisition performance and ensure seamless operational and financial alignment. Risk Management & Governance
• Oversee corporate risk frameworks, including financial, operational, and compliance risks.
• Manage banking relationships, credit facilities, and capital structure optimization.
• Ensure adherence to regulatory, tax, and industry-specific financial requirements.
• Support board reporting, audit processes, and governance standards. Leadership & Team Development
• Lead and mentor the finance team, fostering a culture of accountability, clarity, and continuous improvement.
• Collaborate closely with operations, HR, safety, and business development to ensure financial alignment across the organization.
• Champion S.E.M.’s values and contribute to a strong, people-first leadership culture.
Requirements

Who You Are:

A senior finance executive with 10–15+ years of progressive experience in a construction or large project-based environment.
• Proven experience leading M&A transactions, including due diligence, valuation, deal negotiation, and integration.
• Deep understanding of construction financials: WIP, job costing, bonding, risk, and multi-project forecasting.
• A strategic thinker who can operate at both the executive and operational levels. • A relationship-builder who communicates clearly, collaborates naturally, and leads with integrity.
• Someone who thrives in a growing, entrepreneurial environment and wants to help shape a company’s future.
• Educational Foundation: Holds an advanced academic background such as a dual degree in law and business (e.g., JD/MBA from the Ivey Business School) or an equivalent combination of legal and financial education supporting sophisticated dealmaking, corporate governance, and strategic growth. Compensation & Executive Package S.E.M. Construction offers a high-calibre executive compensation package designed to attract and retain exceptional leadership talent.
• Competitive Executive Salary:
Commensurate with experience leading finance in large construction environments and managing complex M&A transactions.
• Performance-Based Incentives:
Annual bonus structure tied to corporate financial performance, strategic growth milestones, and successful execution of acquisition or integration initiatives.

jobs.description:
Location: Toronto- Hybrid (3 days onsite per week)

Yonge-Eglinton

Department: Finance

Status: Full-Time Permanent

Salary Range: $140,000-$150,000 annually

This role supports the healthcare brands across the FH Health portfolio (Pollin Fertility, Perennial and Wellness Haus). FH Health was founded by tech entrepreneurs to support Canada’s pandemic response with innovative healthcare solutions. We’ve since evolved into a leading health-tech company that transforms traditional clinic experiences by integrating diagnostics and care through technology. We are proud to support a portfolio of healthcare brands:

Pollin Fertility-A next-generation fertility centre revolutionizing patient experience, safety, and outcomes through advanced technology.
Perennial – Integrated primary and wellness care brought directly to retirement residences, improving seniors' health and quality of life.
Wellness Haus – A physician-led clinic blending evidence-based medicine with cutting-edge wellness care.

Learn more:
www.fhhealth.com
www.pollinfertility.com
www.perennialcare.ca

About the Role

We are seeking a strategic and hands-on Director of Finance to lead and scale our finance function and support the growth and expansion of the business. This role will serve as a key member of the leadership team, partnering closely with the executive team to drive financial performance, support growth initiatives, and shape the company’s long-term strategy. This role will also champion process improvements, automation, and the adoption of modern financial technologies, including AI-driven tools, to transform and elevate the finance function. The successful candidate will bring a forward-thinking, digitally savvy approach to optimizing workflows, enhancing reporting, and enabling smarter, faster decision-making.The ideal candidate is a designated CPA with strong analytical capabilities and a proven track record of building high-performing teams, optimizing financial operations, and enabling data-driven decision-making in a high-growth environment.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Leadership & Strategy
Act as a strategic advisor to the executive team on financial planning, growth, and expansion initiatives
Lead the development of long-term financial strategy aligned with corporate objectives
Translate business strategy into actionable financial plans and performance metrics
Support capital planning, fundraising, and investor relations as needed

Financial Planning & Analysis
Oversee budgeting, forecasting, and financial modeling across all business units
Review financial results and identify key drivers, risks, and opportunities
Develop insights on profitability levers, cost optimization, and revenue growth
Establish KPIs and dashboards to enable real-time, data-driven decision-making
Partner with operations and clinical leaders to align financial and business strategies

Financial Reporting & Controls
Oversee monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting processes
Ensure accuracy and integrity of financial statements in accordance with ASPE
Strengthen internal controls, policies, and financial governance frameworks
Lead audit processes, tax compliance, and coordination with external advisors
Accounting & Finance OperationsProvide oversight of day-to-day accounting operations, including A/R, A/P, payroll, inventory management and treasury
Drive process improvements, automation, and scalability across finance functions by leveraging modern technologies, including AI, to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and insight generation
Ensure compliance with regulatory, tax, and payroll requirements
Oversee financial operations across a multi-entity organizational structure

Team Leadership
Lead, mentor, and develop the finance team, fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement
Build and scale the finance function to support company growth and expansion
Promote cross-functional collaboration across departments
Act as a change agent to reimagine and modernize the finance function from the ground up, delivering strategic insights and building a nimble, high-impact team

Qualifications

CPA designation (required) in good standing
8–12+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership roles
Experience in healthcare, technology, or high-growth environments
Strong background in financial planning & analysis, reporting, and operational finance
Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive strategic initiatives
Experience with ERP systems (preferably Odoo) and financial reporting tools
Deep understanding of ASPE and IFRS standards
Exceptional analytical, communication, and leadership skills
Hands-on, adaptable, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment

Why Join FH Health (Perennial, Pollin and Wellness Haus)?

You’ll be joining a mission-driven, fast-growing organization that’s reimagining healthcare with innovation at its core. This is a unique opportunity to play a leadership role in shaping the financial future of a company making a meaningful impact on patients’ lives.

Apply Now

We look forward to learning more about you. If you're a strategic finance leader passionate about driving growth and innovation in healthcare, we encourage you to apply.

FH Health is an equal opportunity, affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.If you are an individual with a disability and require a reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the application process, or are limited in the ability or unable to access or use this online application process and need an alternative method for applying, you may contact careteam@perennialcare.ca for assistance.We thank all applicants in advance for their interest in this position, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Leader, Software Product Development Process Transformation – Connected Vehicles
jobs.description:
Reporting to the Connected Vehicle Engineering Director, the Leader, Software Product Development Process Transformation is responsible for evolving the practices, processes, methods, and tools supporting the design, development, integration, and validation of connected vehicle solutions.

In an environment where software is a strategic component of BRP products, you will contribute to the continuous improvement of software engineering practices while ensuring their seamless integration into the overall product development lifecycle. Working closely with software, systems, architecture, integration, validation, and project management teams, you will help enhance product quality, delivery predictability, and organizational efficiency.

You’ll Have The Opportunity To

Define and roll out new software product development processes tailored to a centralized group delivering software solutions across all product lines.
Align working methods across software, systems, architecture, integration, and validation teams.
Drive the implementation of software engineering best practices, requirements management, integration, and validation.
Promote the adoption of methodologies and tools that improve quality, efficiency, and cross-team collaboration.
Establish the transformation roadmap and lead its execution within the Connected Vehicle group, ensuring consistency and compatibility with product line engineering teams' practices.
Develop and track Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure the maturity, efficiency, and quality of development processes.
Train, coach, and support teams and managers through change management and the adoption of new practices.
Support initiatives related to automation, software quality, and continuous improvement.

YOU WILL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE THE FOLLOWING SKILLS AND QUALITIES:

Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field; 12+ years of relevant experience in software development, including significant experience in process definition or transformation.
A strong understanding of the product development lifecycle and cross-disciplinary engineering interactions.
Proven experience in process improvement, organizational transformation, or operational excellence.
Knowledge of modern software development, quality assurance, and continuous integration practices.
Strong leadership, communication, and influencing skills to align multidisciplinary teams around a shared vision.
Clear accountability for delivery and drive to achieve transformation objectives.

Assets That Will Set You Apart

Experience with Atlassian tools (Jira, Confluence) and DevOps platforms (CI/CD pipelines).
Experience in connected vehicles, embedded systems, or the automotive/powersports industry.
Experience managing multi-product projects within an engineering environment.

Do you have other skills? Tell us what makes you unique and why you would be a great addition to the team.

ACKNOWLEDGING THE POWER OF DIVERSITY

BRP is dedicated to nurturing a culture that invites, connects, and propels the ambitions of people of all backgrounds, profiles, beliefs and experiences. Ultimately, the diversity and uniqueness of our people fuel our ingenuity and set the course for the path ahead!

For this reason, we value diversity and we strive to always push each other forward to build an inclusive workplace where every employee feels like they belong, where they can grow and find meaning.

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO)
is an agency where innovation thrives, ideas flourish, and passion drives us to new heights of excellence. Reporting to the Ministry of the Attorney General, the AGCO is responsible for regulating Ontario’s vibrant alcohol, gaming, horse racing, and private retail cannabis sectors in accordance with the principles of honesty and integrity, and in the public interest.

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) is seeking a strategic, collaborative and forward-thinking leader to serve as Director, People and Culture Strategy. Reporting to the Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO), the Director People and Culture Strategy provides enterprise leadership for People and Culture strategy, transformation and modernization, with responsibility for advancing the People Strategic Plan, divisional priorities, enterprise metrics and executive reporting, HR digital enablement, responsible AI adoption, diversity, inclusion and accessibility (DI&A), inclusive leadership and high-performing team leadership.

This role translates enterprise and divisional priorities into practical strategies, roadmaps, implementation plans, performance measures and governance mechanisms that strengthen organizational readiness, workforce planning, evidence-based decision-making and measurable impact across AGCO.

The ideal candidate is a trusted strategic advisor who brings strong judgment, systems thinking and a collaborative leadership style. They are comfortable operating in a complex public-sector environment, balancing long-term transformation with immediate operational priorities, and translating data, risk, workforce trends and stakeholder needs into practical, inclusive and measurable people strategies.

If you are motivated by the opportunity to lead strategic HR transformation, advance responsible digital and AI adoption, strengthen diversity, inclusion and accessibility, and support a strong employee experience, this role offers a meaningful platform to make a lasting enterprise-wide contribution at AGCO.

What You Will Do

Lead the development, implementation and ongoing refresh of AGCO’s People Strategic Plan, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities, government mandates, workforce risks and evolving organizational needs.
Translate organizational priorities into actionable people strategies, roadmaps, initiatives, performance measures and implementation plans.
Oversee the planning, prioritization and delivery of People and Culture initiatives, projects and divisional priorities that advance organizational goals.
Establish planning, governance, reporting and accountability mechanisms to monitor progress against strategic commitments and demonstrate measurable impact.
Provide strategic advice to the CHRO, C-Suite, senior leaders and governance committees on HR priorities, workforce implications, transformation risks and organizational readiness.
Design and oversee enterprise People and Culture performance indicators, dashboards, workforce analytics and executive reporting to support transparency, accountability and evidence-informed decision-making.
Lead HR digital enablement and responsible AI adoption by developing practical capability, governance practices and high-value use cases that improve service quality, efficiency and decision-making.
Provide enterprise leadership for DI&A strategy, accessibility and inclusive leadership, embedding inclusion principles into AGCO culture, operations and people practices.
Lead the refresh, implementation and evaluation of enterprise DI&A strategy, including the development and reporting of meaningful performance measures.
Act as a senior subject matter expert on DI&A and accessibility, advising executives and senior leaders on inclusive talent practices, cultural transformation and emerging obligations.
Provide leadership and direction to a team by setting clear expectations, prioritizing deliverables, supporting development and fostering a culture of inclusion, accountability, learning and high

You Have

Post-secondary education in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Organizational Psychology, Adult Education, Strategic Planning, Leadership, Human Rights, Public Policy or a related field, or equivalent work experience; a master’s degree is considered an asset.
Minimum of 8 years progressive leadership experience in strategic planning, organizational transformation, HR strategy, performance measurement, workforce analytics, DI&A, accessibility, digital enablement and/or related areas.
Demonstrated ability to translate enterprise priorities into practical strategies, roadmaps, governance structures, implementation plans and measurable outcomes.
Strong understanding of HR digital adoption, HRIS-enabled process improvement, workflow automation, workforce analytics, digital service delivery, change management and responsible AI use.
Knowledge of HR data governance, privacy, accessibility, security, records management and ethical use of workforce information.
Experience developing executive-level reports, dashboards, briefings and presentations that translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations.
Strong consultation, facilitation, public speaking and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence and build alignment across senior leaders, governance bodies and cross-functional partners.
Demonstrated experience leading DI&A strategy, accessibility initiatives, inclusive leadership development, employee engagement forums, committees or enterprise-wide measurement frameworks.
Strong knowledge of Ontario legal and regulatory frameworks related to human rights, accessibility, employment standards and inclusive workplace practices.
Experience leading, coaching and developing teams in a complex, unionized and public-sector environment is an asset.
Eligibility to work in Canada and the ability to successfully complete a criminal background check.

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) is an Ontario provincial regulatory agency that reports to the Ministry of the Attorney General. Position Summary

Reporting to the CEO, the Director, Finance will be an important and integral part of the Leadership Team. Director, Finance will lead Dixon Hall's financial management function, providing strategic and operational oversight of accounting, budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and internal controls across the Agency. The Director ensures the financial integrity of Dixon Hall's operations, safeguards its resources, and provides senior management and the Board with the financial insight needed to support sound decision-making in service of Dixon Hall's mission.

The Director, Finance will also liaise with the Board and participate in Board meetings, work with the Chair of the Finance Audit and Risk Committee, and other Board committees as required; undertake and update the Risk portfolio for the agency and manage the finance department in the areas of accounts payable; confirm the accuracy of monthly remittances; record deposits to accounts receivable as well as; you will be responsible for the annual audit working papers and the work required by the finance department to coordinate the annual audit as well as ensuring timely and accurate invoicing; update and maintain the accuracy of the internal database(s); ensure the completion of all administrative duties related to the Finance Department.

Duties And Responsibilities

Strategic Financial Leadership

Serve as Dixon Hall's senior financial strategist, translating the Agency's mission and strategic plan into a sound, sustainable financial framework
Advise the CEO and Board on the financial implications of strategic decisions, including program expansion, new funding opportunities, and organizational risk
Build and maintain Dixon Hall's financial sustainability strategy, including reserve fund policy, revenue diversification, and long-term capital planning
Monitor the regulatory and funding landscape (provincial, federal, and municipal) affecting the non-profit and charitable sector, and advise leadership on emerging risks and opportunities

Budgeting, Forecasting & Financial Planning

Lead Agency-wide operational and capital budgeting and forecasting processes, aligning departmental budgets to strategic priorities
Analyze cost and revenue performance against budget across all programs and funding streams to assess financial performance and risk
Investigate budget and reporting variances and lead corrective action in partnership with program leadership
Identify and act on opportunities for cost efficiency and revenue growth across the Agency

Fund Accounting, Funder & Grant Compliance (NPO-specific)

Oversee fund accounting practices to ensure accurate tracking and reporting of restricted and unrestricted funding across all programs and funders (municipal, provincial, federal, and philanthropic)
Ensure compliance with individual funder reporting requirements and deadlines, including government funding agreements administered through Ontario Health Teams and other current provincial/municipal funding bodies
Oversee the integrity of client billing, fee revenue, and accounts receivable processes across program areas, ensuring accurate reconciliation between program systems (e.g., CIMS) and the Agency's accounting system
Oversee the accuracy and timeliness of donation processing and reconciliation between the donor database (e.g., SUMAC) and the accounting system, in partnership with Fund Development

Financial Reporting, Governance & Risk Management

Prepare and present financial statements, variance analyses, and strategic financial reporting to the CEO, Board, and Finance/Audit Committee
Ensure the adequacy and ongoing effectiveness of internal controls across all financial processes
Develop, monitor, and enforce financial policies and procedures governing accounting, budgeting, forecasting, and project/program tracking
Lead the annual external audit process and serve as primary liaison to the Agency's auditors
Ensure timely and accurate charitable regulatory filings (including the CRA T3010 Registered Charity Information Return) and compliance with all applicable non-profit financial regulations

Financial Systems Modernization & Automation

Lead the modernization of Dixon Hall's financial systems and processes, identifying opportunities to automate manual, repetitive tasks (e.g., billing reconciliation, revenue posting, payroll allocation, donation reconciliation) currently performed across CIMS, ADAGIO, and SUMAC
Champion the adoption of integrated, cloud-based financial and reporting tools that reduce manual data entry, minimize reconciliation errors, and free up Finance team capacity for higher-value analysis and strategic support
Evaluate and recommend automation opportunities in funder reporting, program cost allocation, and month-end close processes, balancing efficiency gains against cost, staff capacity, and data security requirements
Partner with IT and external vendors to scope, implement, and change-manage new financial systems or automation tools, ensuring proper internal controls and audit trails are maintained throughout
Build the Finance team's digital capability, ensuring staff are trained and equipped to work effectively with new tools and systems as automation is introduced

Payroll & Vendors & CRA Financial Oversight

Ensure accurate accrual and allocation of payroll & vendor costs, including benefits allocation by program and funding source
Oversee accurate program-based cost allocation for government and third-party funded positions
Ensure payroll-related financial reporting (including CRA remittance reconciliation) is accurate and current
Ensure CRA compliance on all financial matters

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, develop, and supervise the Finance department, fostering a culture of accuracy, accountability, and continuous improvement
Hire, train, coach, and formally evaluate Finance team members
Build team capability to support the Agency's growing scale and complexity

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Organizational Impact

Partners with Directors and program leaders across Dixon Hall to ensure financial decisions support — and are informed by — operational and client-service realities
Champion a client-focused, mission-driven approach to financial management, recognizing Finance's role in enabling Dixon Hall's community impact
Drive process improvements and technology modernization (accounting systems, reporting tools) to increase efficiency and data reliability across the Agency

Qualifications

CPA, CGA, College Diploma in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or a related field or equivalent senior level financial experience
10-15 years of experience in Finance with 10 years in managerial positions
Ability to oversee and manage teams
Experience with budgets, accounting, and reporting systems
Strong working knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles
Proficiency with a variety of accounting software, CIMS for billings and SUMAC accounting software and spreadsheet programs and applications
Effective attention to detail and a high degree of accuracy
Ability to build and maintain lasting internal and external relationships
High level of proficiency with Microsoft Office productivity suite
Knowledge and experience with office operational equipment
Experience with not for profit funding and reporting
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a strong ability to exchange knowledge
Strong verbal and written English language communication skills; fluency in additional languages, relevant to the Agency’s communities of service, will be considered an asset
Must be qualified to work in Canada legally for the employer
Able to provide a Vulnerable Sector Screening check with a ‘Clear’ or satisfactory result that meets the operational requirements of the Agency

Working Conditions

Modern office workspace illuminated by either fluorescent, LED, incandescent, or natural light sources
Able to access older buildings and workspaces that have not been converted to meet current accessibility standards
Quiet to moderate noise levels that are consistent with a modern office space in which multiple employees work simultaneously
Overtime as required

Physical and Sensory Demands

Long periods spent at a desk/computer
Manual dexterity required to use desktop computer and peripherals
Able to tolerate a variety of indoor environments as determined by program location
Mobility will be a key component of this position in order to address the needs of our Agency locations and programs

This role supports the healthcare brands across the FH Health portfolio (Pollin Fertility, Perennial and Wellness Haus). We’ve since evolved into a leading health-tech company that transforms traditional clinic experiences by integrating diagnostics and care through technology. We are proud to support a portfolio of healthcare brands:

Pollin Fertility-A next-generation fertility centre revolutionizing patient experience, safety, and outcomes through advanced technology.
Perennial – Integrated primary and wellness care brought directly to retirement residences, improving seniors' health and quality of life.
Wellness Haus – A physician-led clinic blending evidence-based medicine with cutting-edge wellness care.

www.fhhealth.com

www.perennialcare.ca

About the Role

We are seeking a strategic and hands-on Director of Finance to lead and scale our finance function and support the growth and expansion of the business. This role will serve as a key member of the leadership team, partnering closely with the executive team to drive financial performance, support growth initiatives, and shape the company’s long-term strategy. This role will also champion process improvements, automation, and the adoption of modern financial technologies, including AI-driven tools, to transform and elevate the finance function. The successful candidate will bring a forward-thinking, digitally savvy approach to optimizing workflows, enhancing reporting, and enabling smarter, faster decision-making.The ideal candidate is a designated CPA with strong analytical capabilities and a proven track record of building high-performing teams, optimizing financial operations, and enabling data-driven decision-making in a high-growth environment.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Leadership & Strategy
Act as a strategic advisor to the executive team on financial planning, growth, and expansion initiatives
Lead the development of long-term financial strategy aligned with corporate objectives
Translate business strategy into actionable financial plans and performance metrics
Support capital planning, fundraising, and investor relations as needed

Financial Planning & Analysis
Oversee budgeting, forecasting, and financial modeling across all business units
Review financial results and identify key drivers, risks, and opportunities
Develop insights on profitability levers, cost optimization, and revenue growth
Establish KPIs and dashboards to enable real-time, data-driven decision-making
Partner with operations and clinical leaders to align financial and business strategies

Financial Reporting & Controls
Oversee monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting processes
Ensure accuracy and integrity of financial statements in accordance with ASPE
Strengthen internal controls, policies, and financial governance frameworks
Lead audit processes, tax compliance, and coordination with external advisors
Accounting & Finance OperationsProvide oversight of day-to-day accounting operations, including A/R, A/P, payroll, inventory management and treasury
Drive process improvements, automation, and scalability across finance functions by leveraging modern technologies, including AI, to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and insight generation
Ensure compliance with regulatory, tax, and payroll requirements
Oversee financial operations across a multi-entity organizational structure

Team Leadership
Lead, mentor, and develop the finance team, fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement
Build and scale the finance function to support company growth and expansion
Promote cross-functional collaboration across departments
Act as a change agent to reimagine and modernize the finance function from the ground up, delivering strategic insights and building a nimble, high-impact team

Qualifications

CPA designation (required) in good standing
8–12+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership roles
Experience in healthcare, technology, or high-growth environments
Strong background in financial planning & analysis, reporting, and operational finance
Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive strategic initiatives
Experience with ERP systems (preferably Odoo) and financial reporting tools
Deep understanding of ASPE and IFRS standards
Exceptional analytical, communication, and leadership skills
Hands-on, adaptable, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment

Why Join FH Health (Perennial, Pollin and Wellness Haus)?

You’ll be joining a mission-driven, fast-growing organization that’s reimagining healthcare with innovation at its core. This is a unique opportunity to play a leadership role in shaping the financial future of a company making a meaningful impact on patients’ lives.

Apply Now

We look forward to learning more about you. If you're a strategic finance leader passionate about driving growth and innovation in healthcare, we encourage you to apply.

In an environment where software is a strategic component of BRP products, you will contribute to the continuous improvement of software engineering practices while ensuring their seamless integration into the overall product development lifecycle. Working closely with software, systems, architecture, integration, validation, and project management teams, you will help enhance product quality, delivery predictability, and organizational efficiency.

You’ll Have The Opportunity To

Define and roll out new software product development processes tailored to a centralized group delivering software solutions across all product lines.
Align working methods across software, systems, architecture, integration, and validation teams.
Drive the implementation of software engineering best practices, requirements management, integration, and validation.
Promote the adoption of methodologies and tools that improve quality, efficiency, and cross-team collaboration.
Establish the transformation roadmap and lead its execution within the Connected Vehicle group, ensuring consistency and compatibility with product line engineering teams' practices.
Develop and track Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure the maturity, efficiency, and quality of development processes.
Train, coach, and support teams and managers through change management and the adoption of new practices.
